home.introHeading: a local network, real leadership, lasting impact
home.introBody: Built for girls in the ACT region, The Girls Leadership Network connects students across schools and communities into a supportive leadership community. This is not a one-off workshop. It is an ongoing growth experience, focused on practical leadership skills girls can use straight away in classrooms, teams, projects and everyday life.

columns.heading: the program
columns.body: Places are capped on purpose, so every girl is known and every voice gets airtime.
items: Six monthly interactive leadership workshops
Small-group cohorts built for real connection
Age-aligned curriculum
In-person sessions across Canberra
Guest speakers and changemakers from the ACT community
Hands-on leadership activities, not lectures

columns.heading: what girls gain
columns.body: Girls do not just learn leadership at TGLN. They practise it.
items: Confident communication and public speaking
Decision-making and problem solving
Emotional intelligence and resilience
Values-based leadership
Collaboration and team leadership
Initiative and project ownership

columns.heading: why schools choose us
columns.body: We work alongside Canberra schools and families to strengthen leadership pathways for girls across the region.
items: Locally grounded and community connected
Skills aligned with future-ready capabilities
Safe, structured, professionally facilitated sessions
Focus on both confidence and character
Strong peer and mentor support

ourStory.title: our story
ourStory.heading: why we created the girls leadership network
body: Our founder, Ritu Clementi, ran similar programs with the Red Cross in North Carolina and Georgia in the United States. They were a success, and they won several accolades including the Martin Luther King Jr Diversity award from Nike.

After moving to Canberra, Ritu found there were few long-term programs for senior girls across the ACT. She received a Great Ydeas grant in May 2016 to start one, and began building it with her daughter Asha, who was also the target audience.

Asha and Ritu brought in founding volunteers: Wendy Marman on the initial leadership content, alongside Sian Rinaldi, Ladan Amirazizi and Catherine McGufficke. In 2020 we opened a Sydney chapter, led by TGLN alum Gabrielle Murphy. In 2025 Alison McCarthy and Rachel O’Connor joined as session coordinators for the Canberra chapter.

theNetwork.title: the network
theNetwork.heading: the network
theNetwork.intro: The Girls Leadership Network was founded in 2017. Each year a new group of young women comes together to build their skills and their networks. These are some of the reasons they told us they joined.
reasons: My personal leadership goal is to be more self-assured and confident in my ability to communicate to others.
I’m hoping to learn how to grow in leadership with other girls, and how to inspire and encourage one another.
I’m a college captain of a big school, so I would love to learn how to be myself while still leading a large team.
I hope to hear from a range of speakers about their leadership experiences, especially people who have come from different places.
Growing up is hard. You’re always being influenced by the media and other people’s opinions, so stepping out of your comfort zone to be a leader and not a follower can be a challenge.

grtw.title: girls run the world
grtw.heading: girls run the world
grtw.intro: Founded in 2017, Girls Run the World gives young leaders aged 18 to 25 a day in the life of an embassy staff member.
body: Working alongside embassy staff, a participant’s day might include discussing humanitarian issues, meeting the ambassador, planning the agenda for a business delegation, or running the embassy’s social media.
Experiencing embassy work first hand, participants build connections in the field as they work towards their own goals. The program has grown to more than 30 participants across 15 embassies.
grtw.goalsHeading: what the takeover day sets out to do
goals: Share knowledge across cultures and give young women real exposure to diplomacy
Introduce embassies to a wider Australian audience and support their social impact work
Put young women in situations where they make, influence or inform a real decision
grtw.hanBody: In November 2019 The Girls Leadership Network received Hän Honours from the Republic of Finland, recognising the collaboration between TGLN and the Embassy of Finland that created Girls Run the World. The Hän Honours go to organisations working to build a more equal world.

getInvolved.title: get involved
getInvolved.heading: get involved
getInvolved.intro: The Girls Leadership Network runs on the support, insight and energy of our community. Whether you teach, speak, lead an organisation or came through the program yourself, there is a way in.

ways.heading: educators
ways.body: You see the potential in your students every day, and you know which girls are ready to step up.
items: Spot and nominate students who show leadership promise
Share TGLN programs and opportunities with your cohorts
Support girls through workshops, mentoring and hands-on projects
Build confidence, collaboration and initiative inside your school

ways.body: Share what you know with girls who are ready to lead. We are looking for industry leaders, changemakers, politicians, community figures and subject experts who will run an interactive session.
items: Lead a workshop on your area of expertise
Sit on a panel and answer real questions
Mentor girls through a leadership challenge

ways.heading: alumni
ways.body: Once a TGLN girl, always part of the network. Alumni share what they learned and show the next cohort what is possible.

Stay connected with the network as your career takes shape

ways.body: Every contribution strengthens the network. Partnership can be financial, in-kind, or the loan of a room and a few good people.

Provide in-kind support such as venues, catering or printing

posts.title: gamification and motivation with Kerstin Oberprieler
posts.author: Gabi Murphy
posts.summary: Kerstin Oberprieler on turning goals into games, and why anything you can measure you can turn into motivation.
body: This episode is available as a podcast. You can listen on our host platform, or on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Our first episode is with Kerstin Oberprieler, co-founder and CEO of PentaQuest. PentaQuest works on employee engagement through gamification, which uses game mechanics and experience design to get people solving problems. Gamification takes mechanics such as goals, avatars and points, and uses them to shift behaviour.

Kerstin credits her interest in gamification to her love of teamwork, her psychology and commerce background, and her time at Australian consulting firm ThinkPlace. After using gamification at ThinkPlace she went on to complete a PhD in it, then started PentaQuest so other organisations could use it too.
PentaQuest works with large teams and processes, but gamification also works at an individual level. You can use it for exercise, study or savings. Anything you can measure, you can turn into a game.
Ticking items off a list is gamification, because a list is a progress bar. So is tracking your steps on a watch, or charting your savings towards a goal.

childSafety.title: child safety
childSafety.heading: our commitment to child safety
childSafety._help: REVIEW BEFORE LAUNCH. Confirm the wording with your leadership team and update the placeholders in square brackets.
childSafety.intro: The Girls Leadership Network is committed to the safety, wellbeing and participation of every young person in our programs. We have zero tolerance for child abuse and harm of any kind.

sections.heading: how we keep girls safe
items: All facilitators, session coordinators and volunteers who work directly with participants hold a current ACT Working with Vulnerable People registration.
Sessions are run in supervised venues with at least two adults present at all times.
Guest speakers are briefed on our expectations before every session and are not left unsupervised with participants.
We follow the National Principles for Child Safe Organisations.

sections.heading: photos and media
items: We ask a parent or guardian for written consent before we photograph or film a participant.
Consent can be withdrawn at any time by emailing us, and we will remove the image from our website and social media.
We never publish a participant’s full name alongside a photograph without consent.

sections.heading: raising a concern
items: If you have a concern about the safety or wellbeing of a young person in our programs, email us at admin@thegirlsleadershipnetwork.org.
If a child is in immediate danger, call 000.
To report a concern about child abuse or neglect in the ACT, contact Child and Youth Protection Services on 1300 556 729.

privacy.title: privacy
privacy.heading: privacy
privacy._help: REVIEW BEFORE LAUNCH. Replace every placeholder in square brackets. See privacy-policy-draft.md for the full draft and the notes for the leadership team.
privacy.intro: The Girls Leadership Network is a not-for-profit leadership community for girls in the ACT region. Most of the people whose information we hold are under 18, so we treat that information with more care than the law strictly requires of an organisation our size. We handle personal information in line with the Australian Privacy Principles in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

sections.heading: what we collect from participants and their families
items: Name, date of birth, school and year level.
Contact details for the participant and for a parent or guardian, plus an emergency contact.
Health and access information, including allergies, dietary requirements, medical conditions and any support a participant needs to take part.
What a participant tells us about their leadership goals, and any feedback they give us.

sections.heading: what we collect from speakers, volunteers and educators
items: Name, organisation, role and contact details.
Areas of expertise and availability.
Working with Vulnerable People registration number and expiry date, where the role requires one.

sections.heading: sensitive information
items: Health information, disability, cultural background and Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander status are sensitive information under the Privacy Act.
We collect these only where we need them to keep a participant safe or to make a session accessible, and only with consent.
We do not share sensitive information with sponsors, schools or speakers. It goes to the facilitators running the session and no further.

sections.heading: consent, and how it works for young people
items: For participants under 15, we ask a parent or guardian to consent, and we explain to the participant what we are collecting and why.
Participants aged 15 and over can usually consent for themselves. We still keep a parent or guardian informed about registration, health information and emergency arrangements.
Consent is not a one-off. A participant or their family can change their mind at any time by emailing us.

sections.heading: photos, video and social media
items: We ask a parent or guardian for written consent before we photograph or film a participant.
Photo consent is separate from program registration. Saying no to photos does not affect a place in the program.
We do not publish a participant’s full name alongside a photograph.

You can withdraw consent at any time by emailing admin@thegirlsleadershipnetwork.org. We will remove the image from our website and social media within [10 business days]. Printed material already distributed cannot be recalled.

sections.heading: why we collect it
items: To run our programs and keep participants safe.
To communicate with participants and their families about sessions, changes and opportunities.
To match speakers and facilitators to sessions.
To report to sponsors and grant bodies, using numbers and de-identified information only.
We do not sell personal information and we do not use it for advertising.

sections.heading: who we share it with
items: Facilitators and session coordinators get only what they need to run a safe session.
Venues get participant numbers, and health or access information where the venue needs it.
Guest speakers get session numbers and age range. Never contact details or health information.
Sponsors and grant bodies get de-identified reporting. We seek separate consent before using a named testimonial or a photograph.

We use Google Workspace and Google Forms to run our email and registrations, and Vercel to host this website. These providers store information on servers that may be located outside Australia, including in the United States.
We share information where the law requires it, or where there is a risk to someone’s safety. This includes reporting a child protection concern to ACT Child and Youth Protection Services.

sections.heading: how we store it and how long we keep it
items: Records are held in TGLN’s Google Workspace, with access limited to the leadership team members who need it. Accounts use multi-factor authentication.
Participant registration records are kept for [7 years] after a participant’s last program, then deleted.
Health and emergency information is deleted at the end of each program year.
Speaker and volunteer records are kept for [2 years] after last contact.
Photographs are kept while consent stands, and deleted on request.

If information is lost or accessed without authorisation and it is likely to cause serious harm, we will tell the people affected and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner as soon as we can.

sections.heading: this website
items: This site does not use advertising cookies and does not track you across other websites.
Fonts and images are served from our own domain, so loading a page does not send your details to a third party.
Our hosting provider keeps standard server logs, including IP addresses, for security and performance.

sections.heading: getting your information, correcting it, or having it deleted
items: Email the leadership team at admin@thegirlsleadershipnetwork.org and ask. We will respond within [30 days], at no charge.
You can ask us what we hold about you, ask us to correct anything that is wrong, or ask us to delete it unless we are required to keep it.

sections.heading: complaints
items: Email the leadership team at admin@thegirlsleadershipnetwork.org. We will acknowledge your complaint within [5 business days] and answer within [30 days].
If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner at oaic.gov.au or on 1300 363 992.

sections.heading: changes to this policy
items: We review this policy every [12 months]. The current version is always on this page, with the review date at the top.
